summary: Optimization config safety decision-tree: staged rollback and tenant impact mitigation
description: Customer BrightHealth reports latency volatility and a modest accuracy drift after enabling a composite optimizer profile (async-batching + prefix-cache + 8-bit quant). They enabled the profile against their dedicated pool as a staged experiment. They need a low-risk, tenant-safe decision tree to roll back specific features without impacting other orgs on the same Dedicated cluster.
impact: Production latency 95p increased from 120ms to 380ms for BrightHealth routes; error rate of streaming sessions rose from 0.2% to 1.6%; observed slight model token-generation differences in evaluation prompts (~1-2% bleu-style delta). Customer-facing requests are impacted for ~12% of their traffic.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer enabled optimizer profile 'composite-high-throughput-v2' for tenant brighthealth-prod on Dedicated pool RB-07 on 2026-03-11 21:10 UTC
2) Run representative chat workload: 20 concurrent sessions, average prompt length 120 tokens, response lengths ~60 tokens
3) Observe metrics via Console: per-tenant 95p latency and streaming disconnects increase within ~30 minutes
4) Reproduce locally by routing a small percentage (5%) of traffic with same profile using traffic-split in Console
logs: 2026-03-11T21:28:03Z brighthealth-prod requestId=6a7b latency=412ms status=200 model=redwood-open-7b-quantized-8bit optimizer=composite-high-throughput-v2
Console snapshot (2026-03-11T22:00Z): tenant.95p=380ms, tenant.error_rate=1.6%, node.cpu=83%, node.gpu_mem=78%
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: async batching increase + 8-bit quantization interaction produces occasional oversized batches which push GPU memory pressure, triggering KV eviction thrash and stream disconnects.
Telemetry shows per-node KV eviction spikes correlated with higher tail latency. Eviction counts on rb-07-gpu-3 increased by 8x after profile activation.
No cluster-wide capacity alarms; issue appears tenant-scoped but exacerbated on node with higher co-tenancy. BrightHealth runs long sequences which accentuate KV pressure.
Related PR touching batch coalescer heuristics: infra PR #1942 may change batch latency goals under high concurrency — linked for context.

SRE ran a quick canary reverting only async-batching for a single tenant on a single node and observed immediate drop in 95p latency (380ms -> 140ms) within two minutes. Accuracy delta not observed to change in that canary.
Quant profile degradation hypothesis: quantization appears to contribute to GPU memory pressure but not primary cause; combined effect of batching + cache + quant triggers the failure mode.
comments: [2026-03-12 09:10 AM] Marcus Liu (assignee): Acknowledged. Starting with a tenant-local rollback plan to avoid cluster-wide impact. Will coordinate with SRE to schedule a controlled canary at 10:30 UTC.

[2026-03-12 10:45 AM] SRE on-call (Jordan Reyes): Canary revert of async-batching for brighthealth-prod on rb-07-gpu-3 executed. Immediate 95p improvement observed. We captured kernel-level traces and KV eviction histograms; uploading to the incident bucket.

[2026-03-12 13:20 PM] Support (Aisha): Shared step-by-step rollback decision tree and asked customer to hold traffic at 10% while we run the phased plan. Customer agreed to schedule for 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC for full tenant rollout.

[2026-03-13 16:05 PM] Customer (BrightHealth - Jenna Ortiz): Concerned about accuracy impact if we fully disable quantization. Prefers minimal changes that restore latency first. Open to staged approach.
resolution_notes: Planned staged decision-tree executed on 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC with the following ordered steps:
Step A - Preflight: capture snapshot and create tenant config snapshot (done at 2026-03-14 01:48 UTC). Create traffic-split baseline (10% freeze).

Step B - Disable async-batching for tenant only (per-tenant override) and monitor 95p for 10 minutes. Result: 95p reduced from 370ms -> 135ms; error rate reduced to baseline. No measurable accuracy change.
Step C - If Step B failed, next would be temporary prefix-cache throttle (reduce prefetch window). Not required.
Step D - If still failing, revert quant profile to fp16 for tenant only and observe; plan includes a quick A/B shadow compare. Not executed since Step B resolved.
Step E - Gradual traffic ramp and post-mortem: incremented traffic by 25% every 10 minutes, full traffic at 03:10 UTC with stable metrics.

Follow-ups: (1) Infra to land a fix in batch coalescer heuristics (PR #1942) to prevent oversized batching under long-seq tenants; (2) Add automatic per-tenant KV eviction alert to Console; (3) Document recommended preflight test for optimizer-composite profiles (confluence link).
Customer impact: mitigated without reverting quantization; customer acceptance confirmed by Jenna Ortiz 2026-03-14 04:00 UTC.
Ticket status: leave open for two-week observation window; monitoring alert scheduled and follow-up action items assigned to infra and product.
Related artifacts: upload of kernel traces and eviction histograms to S3: s3://redwood-support/brighthealth/sup-999401/ (internal link)
Postmortem action: create an internal RFC to formalize decision-tree for multi-feature optimizer rollbacks and include in runbook library. Assigned INT-43100.
